bull_bear.body:
- Over 7 decades of operating experience as an integrated logistics service provider with expertise across diverse logistics verticals
- Diversified business model spanning mining logistics, CFS, warehousing and allied services that reduces concentration risk associated with any single line of business
- Established mining-logistics capability in mine development support, overburden removal and coal transportation, with ongoing operations for public sector mining companies including Northern Coalfields Limited
- CFS network at three gateway ports (Chennai, Tuticorin, Visakhapatnam) with aggregate handling capacity of 0.4 million TEUs across approximately 325,000 square metres
- Operational and financial backing of ultimate holding company Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects Limited, providing enhanced financial strength, an expanded customer base and cross-selling opportunities across the group
- Completion of the settlement under the NCLT-approved resolution plan, which the Board expects to strengthen the financial position and enhance stakeholder confidence
- Long-duration contracted revenue visibility from the South Eastern Coalfields letter of acceptance, awarded for approximately 11 years and 7 months
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Business concentration in a few large PSU mining contracts — Certain businesses, particularly mining logistics, depend on a limited number of large contracts awarded by government entities and public sector undertakings. Any delay in the award or renewal of contracts, early termination, or reduction in project scope may adversely affect revenue and profitability.
- Dependence on mining sector activity and policy — Mining logistics is a significant component of operations and is exposed to changes in government policy on coal production, mining regulations, environmental clearances and statutory approvals. Delays in commencement of mining projects, lower coal evacuation, adverse weather or disruptions in mining operations may impact equipment utilisation and operating margins.
- Volatility in EXIM trade driving the terminal / CFS business — The terminal business is linked to India's import and export trade. Global slowdown, geopolitical developments, shipping line disruptions, fluctuations in container availability, changes in customs procedures or diversion of cargo to competing ports may adversely affect container volumes and utilisation of CFS infrastructure.
- Fuel price and cost inflation with inadequate contractual escalation — Transportation and logistics operations are significantly influenced by diesel prices, equipment operating costs, labour expenses and maintenance costs. Volatility in fuel prices and inflationary pressures may impact operating margins where contractual escalation mechanisms are inadequate to fully recover increased costs - a point management repeats for mining logistics contracts specifically.
- Regulatory and compliance exposure across a highly regulated footprint — The Company must comply with laws relating to transportation, mining, ports, customs, environmental protection, labour, taxation and corporate governance. Amendments to regulations, increased compliance requirements or delays in obtaining statutory approvals may increase operating costs, affect operational efficiency and delay project execution timelines.
- Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in a fragmented industry — The Indian logistics industry remains highly fragmented, with competition from organised logistics companies, global supply chain operators and regional transport providers. Competitive pricing and margin pressure may affect profitability, particularly in transportation and container logistics; warehousing faces added competition from organised warehousing developers and evolving supply chain models.
- Asset-heavy operational risk - equipment, accidents and network disruption — Operations involve extensive deployment of heavy equipment, transportation assets and cargo handling infrastructure. Equipment breakdowns, accidents, natural disasters, labour shortages, transport network disruptions and supply chain interruptions may impact service delivery and operational performance.
- Financial and liquidity risk, and technology obsolescence — The Company is exposed to liquidity management, interest rate fluctuation, credit and working capital risks, with treasury management and disciplined capital allocation cited as key priorities. Separately, rapid adoption of digital logistics platforms, warehouse automation, AI and data analytics requires continuous technology investment to stay competitive, and increasing digitisation exposes the Company to cyber attack, ransomware and data breach risk.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Incorporated in 1955, Sical is a diversified integrated logistics solutions provider offering overburden removal and coal transportation for mining customers, integrated multimodal logistics and cargo handling, container freight station operations, warehousing and distribution, dredging and other value-added logistics services. Its core service comprises loading, unloading and road transportation executed on a contractual basis, with a primary focus on mining logistics. The Company serves customers in mining, infrastructure, manufacturing, metals, energy, fertilizers, cement, automobiles and consumer goods.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Mining logistics:** Overburden removal and excavation, Coal transportation, Mine development support
- **Terminals / Container Freight Station:** Import-export cargo handling, Container stuffing and de-stuffing, Customs-related services, Cargo storage
- **Integrated logistics:** Multimodal transportation, Cargo handling, Customised supply chain solutions
- **Warehousing and 3PL:** Storage and warehousing, Inventory management, Distribution and value-added logistics
- **Other services:** Dredging

outlook.body:
- Keep mining logistics as a core growth vertical - mine development support, overburden removal, excavation and coal transportation for public sector mining companies
- Improve operational efficiencies, optimise asset utilisation and enhance service delivery to strengthen customer relationships in the integrated logistics and terminals business
- Optimise warehouse utilisation and expand integrated supply chain solutions; modernise and enhance warehousing infrastructure
- Maintain a diversified business model across mining logistics, CFS, warehousing and allied services to reduce concentration risk from any single line of business
- Leverage the Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects group for financial strength, an expanded customer base, operational synergies and cross-selling across mining logistics, rail logistics, warehousing and integrated supply chain solutions
- Focus on operational excellence, cost optimisation, customer satisfaction and prudent resource allocation across all business verticals
- Continue investment in technology and digital infrastructure to stay competitive as digital logistics platforms, warehouse automation, AI and data analytics reshape the sector
- Complete deleveraging/settlement obligations - the final tranche of the resolution amount under the NCLT-approved resolution plan was paid during the year, expected to strengthen the financial position
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Sical's expansion in FY 2025-26 is contract-led rather than greenfield-capex-led. In mining logistics the Company continued to execute the overburden excavation and transportation contract at the Nigahi Open Cast Project in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh, with ongoing operations for Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL), and received a letter of acceptance from South Eastern Coalfields Limited for an overburden excavation and removal project at the Porda Chimtapani Opencast Project in Raigarh, Chhattisgarh, with a contract value of approximately Rs. 403,800 lakh (inclusive of GST) awarded for approximately 11 years and 7 months, which the Board describes as providing a stable and visible revenue baseline over the long term. In the terminals business the Company operates Container Freight Station facilities at Chennai, Tuticorin and Visakhapatnam with an aggregate handling capacity of 0.4 million TEUs spread across approximately 325,000 square metres, and expects increasing containerisation, port capacity augmentation and customs digitisation to improve throughput and asset utilisation across that network. In warehousing and integrated supply chain the Company states it is focused on modernising and enhancing its warehousing infrastructure to improve operational efficiency and customer service, and on expanding integrated supply chain solutions. Management also flags that continuous investment in technology and digital infrastructure is necessary as digital logistics platforms, warehouse automation, AI and data analytics reshape the sector. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum, commissioning schedule or capacity-addition target is disclosed. Note on sourcing: the warehousing-modernisation and technology-investment statements above were read from the MD&A Opportunities and Threats text routed into the profile and risks bundles of this same annual report, not into the capex bundle; the capex bundle's Corporate Overview section is truncated mid-sentence in the CFS paragraph.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Continued growth in domestic coal production, increased power generation capacity and higher infrastructure spending are expected to create sustained demand for specialised mining logistics services
- India's EXIM trade is expected to continue expanding; increasing containerisation, port capacity augmentation and customs digitisation are expected to improve throughput and asset utilisation across the CFS network
- The shift towards organised warehousing, GST-led supply chain optimisation, growth in e-commerce and 3PL, and manufacturing under the Make in India initiative are expected to generate significant demand for integrated warehousing solutions
- Government infrastructure programmes - PM GatiShakti, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Multimodal Logistics Parks and inland waterways - are reducing transit times and lowering logistics costs, translating macro conditions directly into logistics sector expansion
- India's real GDP is estimated to have grown 7.7% in FY 2025-26 versus 7.1% in FY 2024-25, with PFCE and GFCF each growing more than 7.5%, supporting the domestic investment and consumption cycle
- India is emerging as a preferred destination for supply chain investment, reinforcing domestic logistics demand across sectors
- Global growth remains moderated, with output projected at 3% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, and trade fragmentation and geopolitical conflict introducing volatility into energy prices, freight costs and global supply chains
- Group backing from Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects is expected to deliver improved financial strength, an expanded customer base, operational synergies and enhanced execution capabilities
- Letter of acceptance received from South Eastern Coalfields Limited for an overburden excavation and removal project at the Porda Chimtapani Opencast Project, Raigarh, Chhattisgarh, with a contract value of approximately Rs. 403,800 lakh (inclusive of GST), awarded for approximately 11 years and 7 months, described by the Board as providing a stable and visible revenue baseline over the long term
- Continued execution during the year of the contract for excavation and transportation of overburden at the Nigahi Open Cast Project in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh
- Ongoing mining logistics operations for leading public sector mining companies including Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) in Madhya Pradesh

risks.risk: Business concentration in a few large PSU mining contracts
risks.note: Certain businesses, particularly mining logistics, depend on a limited number of large contracts awarded by government entities and public sector undertakings. Any delay in the award or renewal of contracts, early termination, or reduction in project scope may adversely affect revenue and profitability.

risks.risk: Dependence on mining sector activity and policy
risks.note: Mining logistics is a significant component of operations and is exposed to changes in government policy on coal production, mining regulations, environmental clearances and statutory approvals. Delays in commencement of mining projects, lower coal evacuation, adverse weather or disruptions in mining operations may impact equipment utilisation and operating margins.

risks.risk: Volatility in EXIM trade driving the terminal / CFS business
risks.note: The terminal business is linked to India's import and export trade. Global slowdown, geopolitical developments, shipping line disruptions, fluctuations in container availability, changes in customs procedures or diversion of cargo to competing ports may adversely affect container volumes and utilisation of CFS infrastructure.

risks.risk: Fuel price and cost inflation with inadequate contractual escalation
risks.note: Transportation and logistics operations are significantly influenced by diesel prices, equipment operating costs, labour expenses and maintenance costs. Volatility in fuel prices and inflationary pressures may impact operating margins where contractual escalation mechanisms are inadequate to fully recover increased costs - a point management repeats for mining logistics contracts specifically.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure across a highly regulated footprint
risks.note: The Company must comply with laws relating to transportation, mining, ports, customs, environmental protection, labour, taxation and corporate governance. Amendments to regulations, increased compliance requirements or delays in obtaining statutory approvals may increase operating costs, affect operational efficiency and delay project execution timelines.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in a fragmented industry
risks.note: The Indian logistics industry remains highly fragmented, with competition from organised logistics companies, global supply chain operators and regional transport providers. Competitive pricing and margin pressure may affect profitability, particularly in transportation and container logistics; warehousing faces added competition from organised warehousing developers and evolving supply chain models.

risks.risk: Asset-heavy operational risk - equipment, accidents and network disruption
risks.note: Operations involve extensive deployment of heavy equipment, transportation assets and cargo handling infrastructure. Equipment breakdowns, accidents, natural disasters, labour shortages, transport network disruptions and supply chain interruptions may impact service delivery and operational performance.

risks.risk: Financial and liquidity risk, and technology obsolescence
risks.note: The Company is exposed to liquidity management, interest rate fluctuation, credit and working capital risks, with treasury management and disciplined capital allocation cited as key priorities. Separately, rapid adoption of digital logistics platforms, warehouse automation, AI and data analytics requires continuous technology investment to stay competitive, and increasing digitisation exposes the Company to cyber attack, ransomware and data breach risk.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sical Logistics is one of India's established integrated logistics service providers with over 7 decades of experience in end-to-end supply chain and logistics solutions, now backed by the Pristine Logistics group.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 1955, Sical is a diversified integrated logistics solutions provider offering overburden removal and coal transportation for mining customers, integrated multimodal logistics and cargo handling, container freight station operations, warehousing and distribution, dredging and other value-added logistics services. Its core service comprises loading, unloading and road transportation executed on a contractual basis, with a primary focus on mining logistics. The Company serves customers in mining, infrastructure, manufacturing, metals, energy, fertilizers, cement, automobiles and consumer goods.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Mining logistics:** Overburden removal and excavation, Coal transportation, Mine development support
- **Terminals / Container Freight Station:** Import-export cargo handling, Container stuffing and de-stuffing, Customs-related services, Cargo storage
- **Integrated logistics:** Multimodal transportation, Cargo handling, Customised supply chain solutions
- **Warehousing and 3PL:** Storage and warehousing, Inventory management, Distribution and value-added logistics
- **Other services:** Dredging

end_markets.body:

- Infrastructure

- Automobiles

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued growth in domestic coal production, increased power generation capacity and higher infrastructure spending are expected to create sustained demand for specialised mining logistics services
- India's EXIM trade is expected to continue expanding; increasing containerisation, port capacity augmentation and customs digitisation are expected to improve throughput and asset utilisation across the CFS network
- The shift towards organised warehousing, GST-led supply chain optimisation, growth in e-commerce and 3PL, and manufacturing under the Make in India initiative are expected to generate significant demand for integrated warehousing solutions
- Government infrastructure programmes - PM GatiShakti, Dedicated Freight Corridors, Multimodal Logistics Parks and inland waterways - are reducing transit times and lowering logistics costs, translating macro conditions directly into logistics sector expansion
- India's real GDP is estimated to have grown 7.7% in FY 2025-26 versus 7.1% in FY 2024-25, with PFCE and GFCF each growing more than 7.5%, supporting the domestic investment and consumption cycle
- India is emerging as a preferred destination for supply chain investment, reinforcing domestic logistics demand across sectors
- Global growth remains moderated, with output projected at 3% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, and trade fragmentation and geopolitical conflict introducing volatility into energy prices, freight costs and global supply chains
- Group backing from Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects is expected to deliver improved financial strength, an expanded customer base, operational synergies and enhanced execution capabilities
- Letter of acceptance received from South Eastern Coalfields Limited for an overburden excavation and removal project at the Porda Chimtapani Opencast Project, Raigarh, Chhattisgarh, with a contract value of approximately Rs. 403,800 lakh (inclusive of GST), awarded for approximately 11 years and 7 months, described by the Board as providing a stable and visible revenue baseline over the long term
- Continued execution during the year of the contract for excavation and transportation of overburden at the Nigahi Open Cast Project in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh
- Ongoing mining logistics operations for leading public sector mining companies including Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) in Madhya Pradesh

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Keep mining logistics as a core growth vertical - mine development support, overburden removal, excavation and coal transportation for public sector mining companies
- Improve operational efficiencies, optimise asset utilisation and enhance service delivery to strengthen customer relationships in the integrated logistics and terminals business
- Optimise warehouse utilisation and expand integrated supply chain solutions; modernise and enhance warehousing infrastructure
- Maintain a diversified business model across mining logistics, CFS, warehousing and allied services to reduce concentration risk from any single line of business
- Leverage the Pristine Logistics & Infraprojects group for financial strength, an expanded customer base, operational synergies and cross-selling across mining logistics, rail logistics, warehousing and integrated supply chain solutions
- Focus on operational excellence, cost optimisation, customer satisfaction and prudent resource allocation across all business verticals
- Continue investment in technology and digital infrastructure to stay competitive as digital logistics platforms, warehouse automation, AI and data analytics reshape the sector
- Complete deleveraging/settlement obligations - the final tranche of the resolution amount under the NCLT-approved resolution plan was paid during the year, expected to strengthen the financial position

In warehousing and integrated supply chain the Company states it is focused on modernising and enhancing its warehousing infrastructure to improve operational efficiency and customer service, and on expanding integrated supply chain solutions. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths

- Diversified business model spanning mining logistics, CFS, warehousing and allied services that reduces concentration risk associated with any single line of business
